impl.summary:
Worktree was cut from 683f272 (lacked 1a45970): reset --hard to 1a45970 first, as instructed.

SERVER
- portal/src/server/auth/password.ts: new exported verifyUserPassword(userId, password) (DB lookup + verifyPassword; an account without a hash never matches).
- portal/src/server/actions/profile.ts: module-private checkPassword keeps its pw-confirm rate limit and now calls verifyUserPassword; startTotp/confirm/disable/regenerate/changePasswordAction unchanged otherwise.
- portal/src/server/auth/step-up.ts (new): stepUp(viewer, password, action) → "rateLimited" | "wrongPassword" | null. Per-ACTOR limit `step-up:${v.user.id}` 10 per 15 min (checked before the hash so a limited actor is refused even with the right password), every refusal audited as security.step_up_failed with meta { action, error }.
- portal/src/server/actions/people.ts: resetTwoFactorAction(userId, password) steps up first thing after actionViewer; createLinkAction(userId, kind, password?) steps up for kind "reset" only (invite links unchanged); changeRoleAction(userId, role, password?) returns { ok: true } without a password when the role is unchanged, steps up otherwise. NOTE: the brief named "the role change in updatePersonAction"; in this codebase updatePersonAction has no role field, the role change lives in changeRoleAction, so the step-up went there. All existing audit() entries and the super_admin reach rules are kept. The old hand-written in-app notification in resetTwoFactorAction is replaced by notifyTakeover (keys admin.person.twoFactorResetTitle/Body removed from the ten locales as now unused).
- portal/src/server/services/notify.ts: notifyTakeover(db, tenantId, actor, target, kind, reason?) → notifyUsers to the target (in-app notice with href /profile + email, statuses active/invited) with the new FIXED_MESSAGES kind, and, when the target is a tenant_admin, an in-app "security" notice (href /admin/users/<id>, text admin.person.<kind>Peer with {actor} and {name}, in each peer's language via createTranslator/messagesFor) to every other active tenant_admin except the target and the actor. Role change passes the localized new role name as {{reason}}; a promotion to tenant_admin also notifies peers.
- portal/src/lib/tenant-defaults.ts: FIXED_MESSAGES gains twoFactorReset, resetLinkIssued, roleChanged in ten locales (placeholders {{name}}, {{organisation}}, {{link}}, {{reason}} for roleChanged; in-code-locales test passes); defaultSettings adds security: { supportAccessUntil: null }; withDefaults merges security over the default.
- portal/src/server/db/schema.ts: TenantSettings.security: { supportAccessUntil: string | null } (jsonb, type-only; no migration).
- portal/src/server/services/audit.ts: new actions security.step_up_failed, support.access_granted, support.access_revoked (labels admin.auditActions.* in ten locales; server-helpers label test passes).
- portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts: grantSupportAccessAction() (now + 72 h, audited support.access_granted with meta.until) and revokeSupportAccessAction() (null, audited support.access_revoked), via the existing row-locked saveSettings.
- portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts: adminLinkAction(tenantId, userId, password) steps up first, then reads the target tenant's settings and refuses with error "supportAccess" unless now < supportAccessUntil; the existing platform.admin_link audit stays; the administrator gets the resetLinkIssued notice and the organisation's other administrators the peer notice.

UI
- portal/src/components/admin/person-actions.tsx: exported ConfirmPasswordField (label admin.person.confirmPassword, hint, type=password, autocomplete current-password, aria-invalid/aria-describedby on the Field's -error/-hint ids) and useStepUpError(); the role and 2FA dialogs became forms with the password field; the reset link now opens a confirm dialog (title/body admin.person.resetLinkTitle/Body) with the password field. Invite link unchanged.
- portal/src/components/admin/people-client.tsx: per-row reset link opens the same dialog (one Dialog under the table, state resetFor); uses admin.person keys.
- portal/src/components/admin/platform-client.tsx: admin-link dialog body is a form with the password field (footer button submits it via form=); errors wrongPassword/rateLimited on the field, supportAccess as a toast (admin.platform.supportAccessMissing).
- portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx + src/app/(admin)/admin/settings/page.tsx: new "security" tab (LifeBuoy icon, settings.tabs.security) with SecurityTab: state pill (allowed until <date, formatted on the server> / not allowed), "Allow Safarov Industries support access for 72 hours" and "Revoke" buttons.
- portal/src/app/(admin)/super/page.tsx: per-organisation pill "Support access allowed until {date}" / "Support access not allowed" (requestNow() for the comparison, server-formatted date).
- Messages: admin.json (person, platform, auditActions) and settings.json (tabs.security, security.*) in az en ru tr ro ka uk de fr ar; i18n parity test passes; wording follows the existing translations of the same terms (parol / iki addımlı doğrulama, etc.).

TESTS
- portal/tests/step-up.test.ts (new, real PGlite): wrong password refused + audited and target untouched; right password resets 2FA, notifies the target (in-app + mail subject) and the peer admin (not the actor); learner target → no peer notice; 11th attempt after 10 failures → rateLimited even with the right password; invite link needs no password, reset link does, target notified; same-role change needs no password and no audit, real change refused with wrong password, accepted with the right one, mail names the new role, promotion to tenant_admin notifies peers; operator link refused with wrong password and without a grant (no link issued, step-up failure audited in the operator's tenant); grant sets now+72h and audits, operator link then works and notifies; revoke audits and refuses again; an expired grant refuses.
- tests/people-operator.test.ts, tests/auth-security.test.ts, tests/auth.test.ts updated for the new signatures / mock / default key.

ADR (for the orchestrator to record): "Account-takeover tooling (2FA reset, password reset link, role change, operator support link) requires the actor to re-enter their own password, rate limited per actor (10 per 15 minutes) with every refusal audited; the target always receives an in-app notice and an email, and when the target is an administrator every other administrator receives the in-app notice; the operator's reset link became a consented support grant that a tenant administrator opens for 72 hours from Settings → Security and can revoke, both audited and visible in /super. A second-approver (four-eyes) queue was deliberately not built: step-up + notices + audit give the target and their peers the means to detect and reverse a hostile action within minutes, while a mandatory approver is a separation-of-duties policy choice that depends on each customer's governance (who may approve, what happens with a single administrator, SLA for break-glass) and would add a pending-actions workflow, so it stays an owner decision; the stepUp helper and notifyTakeover are the extension points if it is wanted later."

PROGRESS line: "S-06 closed (B1-takeover): step-up password + per-actor rate limit on 2FA reset / reset link / role change / operator link, target and peer-admin notices, tenant-granted 72-hour support window (Settings → Security, /super), audit entries security.step_up_failed, support.access_granted/revoked; tests in tests/step-up.test.ts."

Checks: npm run typecheck ✓, eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0 ✓, vitest: touched files ✓ and the full suite 111 files / 3005 tests ✓ (after fixing the defaultSettings shape assertion in tests/auth.test.ts). Nothing under portal/drizzle changed.
impl.left_open: Owner decisions / notes: (1) The brief's "role change in updatePersonAction" does not exist here; the step-up was applied to changeRoleAction (the only role-changing action) and the same-role call short-circuits without a password. (2) Peer notices exclude the acting administrator as well as the target (the actor knows what they did); say if the actor should be included. (3) Second-approver queue intentionally not built, see ADR paragraph in summary. (4) The grant is a single 72-hour window per organisation (granting again simply moves the end to now+72h); no per-administrator scoping. (5) Reset-link emails go to the target even when the organisation's own SMTP is off (platform transport / logged outbox), which matches other fixed notices. (6) Audit page: new actions appear in the filter automatically. No new dependency, no migration. Not checked in the running app (no dev server started per the rules); UI verified by typecheck/lint only.
migrations: None: TenantSettings.security.supportAccessUntil is a type-only change inside the existing tenants.settings jsonb column (withDefaults supplies { supportAccessUntil: null }); nothing under portal/drizzle changed.

findings.problem: The step-up is bypassed through the invite kind. createLinkAction only steps up for kind 'reset'; for kind 'invite' it never checks the target's status, and target() (people.ts:43-48) only excludes deleted people, so an administrator with people.write can call the server action directly with createLinkAction(<active admin id>, 'invite') and no password. issueAccountLink (auth/links.ts) has no status check and mints a 14-day invite token for any user; the account page (app/(auth)/account/[kind]/[token]/page.tsx) and setPassword (actions/auth.ts:468-495) accept an invite token for an active account and overwrite its passwordHash (status handling at auth.ts:487 only differs for invited users), then invalidate the victim's sessions. Attack: hostile admin A opens DevTools, calls createLinkAction(B.id, 'invite'), opens the returned /account/invite/<token> link, sets a new password and signs in as B (immediately when B has no 2FA; otherwise B is at least locked out of their own password). No step-up, no 'security.step_up_failed' trail, no notifyTakeover (invite links send nothing), audit shows only the innocuous 'person.invite_link'. The UI only offers the invite button for status 'invited', but the server is the trust boundary. This is exactly S-06's threat and the brief's exemption ('invite links for never-activated accounts stay as they are') only holds if the server restricts invites to never-activated accounts.
findings.fix: In createLinkAction, after target(): `if (kind === "invite" && u.status !== "invited") return { ok: false };` (equivalently route an invite for an activated account through the reset path with the step-up). For defence in depth, make setPassword in actions/auth.ts refuse an invite token whose user is no longer 'invited' (`if (kind === "invite" && row.user.status !== "invited") return { error: "expired" }`) so any stray invite token stops being a password reset once the account is live. Add a test in tests/step-up.test.ts: createLinkAction(learner.id, 'invite') without a password returns { ok: false } and issueAccountLink is not called; bootstrap.ts:110 and emailInvite only target invited accounts, so nothing else breaks.

findings.problem: The target notice is sent only to statuses active/invited, so a suspended person gets neither the in-app notice nor the email. Attack: hostile admin suspends the target (audited, but the suspended person is signed out and sees nothing), mints a reset link with their own password (step-up still required), sets the password, reactivates the account and signs in; the target never receives the 'a reset link was created' email that this package exists to deliver. Peer admins are still notified for a tenant_admin target, which limits the damage, and the sequence is fully audited, so this is minor.
findings.fix: Pass statuses ['active', 'invited', 'suspended'] for the takeover kinds in notifyTakeover (notifyUsers' statuses type needs 'suspended' added), or refuse resetTwoFactorAction/createLinkAction('reset') for suspended targets; one assertion in tests/step-up.test.ts that a suspended target still gets the email.

findings.problem: The per-actor counter is incremented on every call, including successful step-ups, so an administrator who performs 10 legitimate takeover actions in 15 minutes (e.g. role changes during an onboarding) is locked out with 'rateLimited' although they never typed a wrong password. The brief said '10 per 15 minutes' without specifying failures-only, so this is acceptable; just making sure it is a deliberate choice (it also throttles a hijacked session, which is a mild benefit).
findings.fix: Either leave as is and record it in the ADR text ("10 attempts, successful ones included"), or count only failures by calling rateLimit after verifyUserPassword fails plus a separate read-only check before.

reviews.notes:
Reviewed commit 7d76156 on worktree-wf_42496c94-3d0-1 read-only (git show + surrounding code). Verified in the implementer's worktree: `npm run typecheck` passes, `npx eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0` passes, `npx vitest run tests/step-up.test.ts tests/people-operator.test.ts tests/auth.test.ts tests/auth-security.test.ts tests/i18n.test.ts` passes (5 files, 289 tests). Nothing under portal/drizzle is in the commit.

What holds up under the attacker lens: stepUp consumes the limit before the hash check (a limited actor is refused even with the right password) and the limiter is an atomic upsert, so two concurrent requests cannot both pass as the 11th; every refusal is audited with the attempted action; verifyUserPassword returns false for accounts without a hash; resetTwoFactorAction steps up before the target lookup; changeRoleAction short-circuits only when the role is unchanged and keeps the self-change and tenant_admin reach rules; adminLinkAction cannot be pointed at the operator's own tenant for self-grant (settings.write is per tenant, no tenant switching in viewer.ts), reads the target tenant's settings through withDefaults so a missing `security` key refuses, and the operator's step-up failure lands in the operator's tenant audit; grant/revoke go through the row-locked saveSettings and every other settings action spreads the stored object so the grant is not silently dropped; notification text is interpolated as ICU values (no injection through names) and the email link is built from appUrl(); updatePersonAction cannot change the email, and phone sign-in is refused for console roles, so there is no password-less takeover of administrators through profile edits. The UI dialogs are real forms with a labelled password input (autocomplete=current-password, aria-invalid/aria-describedby) and the ten locales have key parity (i18n test).

Blocker: the invite-kind bypass in createLinkAction (details and smallest fix in the finding). The rest is minor/nit. Not checked: the running app (no dev server, per the rules) and the full suite (the orchestrator runs it after the merge).

findings.problem: rateLimit() runs on every step-up, successful ones included, so the budget of 10 per 15 minutes covers all takeover actions, not just failed guesses. An administrator who changes roles for 11 people in a row (or resets 2FA during an incident) gets 'rateLimited' with the correct password. The brief asked for '10 per 15 minutes' without saying whether successes count. The profile pw-confirm limiter behaves the same way.
findings.fix: Leave it as it is and note it in left_open, or charge the bucket only on failure: refuse when the actor already has 10 failures in the window, verify the password, and call rateLimit only when the check fails. That needs a read-only peek, which rate-limit.ts does not offer yet. Owner call.

findings.problem: The security.step_up_failed audit row records only meta { action, error }. It has no targetType or targetId, so an investigator cannot tell whose account a run of failed 2FA-reset or reset-link attempts was aimed at. Every caller knows the target id but does not pass it to stepUp.
findings.fix: Add an optional targetId parameter to stepUp(v, password, action, targetId?) and write targetType: 'user', targetId into the audit call. Pass userId from resetTwoFactorAction, createLinkAction, changeRoleAction and adminLinkAction, and assert it in tests/step-up.test.ts.

findings.problem: settings.security.body says support can create a 'one-time sign-in link'. What adminLinkAction actually issues is a password reset link (issueAccountLink(u.id, 'reset')), which lets support set the administrator's password. The administrator granting consent should see that exact effect. The same wording appears in all ten locales.
findings.fix: Say 'one-time password reset link' (and the equivalent in the other nine locales), matching the resetLinkIssued email.

findings.problem: rateLimit uses fixed windows aligned to the epoch. If the 10 failures and the 11th call fall on either side of a 15-minute boundary, the 11th call succeeds and the test fails. The chance is very low (about the test's duration divided by 15 minutes).
findings.fix: Optional: freeze time with vi.useFakeTimers / vi.setSystemTime around the lockout test.

reviews.notes:
I would approve this. Every acceptance item holds when checked against the code, and none of the four findings is a blocker or major.

Checks I ran: the worktree contains 1a45970; typecheck and eslint (--max-warnings=0) are clean; vitest passes on step-up, people-operator, auth-security, auth, i18n, in-code-locales, rtl-logical and server-helpers (761 tests). Nothing under portal/drizzle changed, and no "Aİ" appears in the diff.

Per acceptance item:
- **Step-up:** 2FA reset, the reset link (invite links stay without a password), the role change and the operator link each call stepUp. stepUp is per actor (`step-up:${userId}`), refuses before checking the hash once the limit is hit, returns 'wrongPassword' or 'rateLimited', and audits every refusal as security.step_up_failed.
- **Role change in changeRoleAction:** the brief named updatePersonAction, but that action has no role field. changeRoleAction is the only path that changes a role (grep found no import upsert and no SCIM role path), so putting the step-up there is right. A call that keeps the same role returns early without a password or an audit row.
- **Notices:** notifyTakeover sends the target an in-app notice and an email through the new FIXED_MESSAGES kinds (ten locales, placeholders filled by notifyUsers). The peer query is active tenant_admins minus the target and the actor. A demotion passes the old role and a promotion the new one, so peers hear of both.
- **Support window:** adminLinkAction reads the target tenant's settings.security.supportAccessUntil and refuses with 'supportAccess' unless the window is still open. Grant and revoke go through the row-locked saveSettings, are audited and refresh the page.
- **Who can grant:** the viewer's tenant comes from the session, so the operator cannot grant consent on a customer's behalf.
- **Visibility:** the grant state is formatted on the server in both the Settings → Security tab and /super, so there is no hydration risk.
- **Dialogs:** they are now forms. The password field has a label, a hint, autocomplete current-password, and aria-invalid / aria-describedby pointing at the Field's own -error / -hint ids. The platform dialog's footer button submits the form via form=.
- **Removed keys:** twoFactorResetTitle/Body are no longer referenced anywhere.
- **Message files:** key parity holds and no message file has a duplicate top-level "security" key.

Not checked: I did not use the UI in a running app, because starting servers is not allowed here. The email-disabled tenant path (queueEmail goes to the logged outbox) is as the implementer described; I did not test it.

Owner decisions still open:
- whether to require a second approver (the ADR paragraph records why it was not built);
- whether the actor should also get the peer notice;
- whether successful step-ups should count against the rate limit (first finding).

impl.summary:
Worktree was cut from 683f272 (lacked 1a45970), so it was reset with `git reset --hard 1a45970` before any work; node_modules linked by junction.

CODE
- portal/src/server/env.ts: optional APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET (both min 32); env.previousSecret and env.domainProofSecret (= APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET ?? APP_SECRET ?? dev secret).
- portal/src/server/crypto.ts: secrets() = [current, previous?] (read from process.env like before, so scripts and tests work without env.ts); kid(secret) = sha256(secret) hex .slice(0,8); encryptSecret writes `v2:<kid>:<iv>:<tag>:<data>`; decryptSecret opens v2 with the key its id names first and then every other key (unknown id falls back), v1 with every key, v1 bytes untouched; new export sealedWithCurrentKey(value) for the rotate script.
- portal/src/server/auth/totp.ts: hashBackupCode(code, secret = env.secret); new backupCodeHashes(code) = [current, previous-key hash when APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS is set, legacy]. portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts spendBackupCode loops over backupCodeHashes.
- portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts: domainProofRecords(tenantId) = [record(env.domainProofSecret), record(env.previousSecret)?]; domainProofFound accepts a string or a list. The published value (domainProofRecordAction) derives from env.domainProofSecret; settings.verifyDomainAction, platform.verifyTenantDomainAction and jobs.recheckDomains check domainProofRecords(). Fixture test pins the existing derivation.
- portal/src/server/db/schema.ts: tenants gets uniqueIndex("tenants_domain_verified_idx").on(domain).where(domain_verified_at is not null). Migration generated locally only (0004_tenant_domain_verified.sql, NOT committed).
- settings.verifyDomainAction and platform.verifyTenantDomainAction: the transaction's unique violation on tenants_domain_verified_idx (isUniqueViolation) returns error "domainTaken" (settings also audits domain.rechecked with meta.taken=true); settings-tabs.tsx and platform-client.tsx toast settings.branding.domainTaken / admin.platform.domainTaken; keys added in all ten locales of messages/*/settings.json and messages/*/admin.json.
- portal/src/server/services/secret-rotation.ts rotateStoredSecrets(db): for every tenant (row locked) re-seals identity.sso.clientSecretEnc, identity.ldap.passwordEnc, email.passwordEnc, integrations.webhookSecretEnc, and users.totp_secret, skipping values already under the current key id (idempotent) and leaving (and counting) values no key opens. portal/scripts/rotate-secret.ts: `npx tsx scripts/rotate-secret.ts`, refuses NODE_ENV=production without a 32+ APP_SECRET, prints counts only.
- scripts/seed-data.ts / seed.ts checked: only the demo organisation carries a verified domain, no change needed.
- Unused env imports removed from jobs.ts and platform.ts (made unused by this change).

DOCS
- docs/OPERATIONS.md: incident 'Contain' bullet now points at the runbook; new section "Rotating APP_SECRET" (generate + escrow, deploy both keys, run the script, remove the old key) plus what is not carried over (signed SSO state, backup codes made before the rotation stop working once APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS is removed, domain proofs unless APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET is set once to the APP_SECRET in use when the records were published).
- portal/README.md: env table rows for APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET, APP_SECRET row and the "APP_SECRET is data" operations note link to the runbook. portal/.env.example documents both variables.

TESTS: portal/tests/crypto.test.ts (new, PGlite): v1 fixture decrypts; v2 kid routing after the key moved to APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS; unknown kid falls back; rotate script re-encrypts 1 tenant + 1 user, leaves current and unreadable values, second run reports zero, values readable after the previous key is removed; backupCodeHashes includes the previous-key hash only during a rotation; domain proof fixture stays, either key's record accepted during rotation; second organisation refused by operator and by its own admin ("domainTaken", row unchanged, partial index allows the unverified same domain); every locale has both messages. tests/auth.test.ts updated to the v2 envelope (5 segments, kid); tests/settings-rate-limit.test.ts mock gains domainProofRecords.

ADR text (for DECISIONS.md): "ADR: APP_SECRET rotation with one previous key. Ciphertexts carry the id (sha256 of the secret, first 8 hex) of the key that sealed them (v2); v1 ciphertexts are opened with every configured key. APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS holds the old key during a rotation and scripts/rotate-secret.ts re-encrypts every stored secret with the current key; no KMS. Domain-proof TXT values derive from APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET (default APP_SECRET), documented as set once and never rotated; during a rotation either key's record is accepted. Signed values are not re-signed. One verified domain per organisation is enforced by the partial unique index tenants_domain_verified_idx; the actions answer domainTaken."

RLS stays a defence-in-depth layer worth its XL cost only where a contract requires database-level isolation; if so, the order is additive tenant_id on child tables, then FORCE RLS with a per-request transaction wrapper.

findings.problem: In a module with more than one lesson, the learner never sees the done screen. With no hash in the URL (the normal first launch), the lesson index is the first unfinished lesson in the `done` state. onComplete calls setDone(session.done()) before the player's own setResult/setPhase('done'), so the index moves on and the `key={`${hash}|${lesson.key}`}` changes. LessonPlayer then remounts on the next lesson's intro, and the result, recap and 'Next lesson' button for the finished lesson are thrown away. After the last lesson every lesson is done, findIndex returns -1, Math.max(0, -1) gives 0, and the learner lands on lesson 1's intro with no sign that the module is complete. The done screen survives only when the learner arrived through a hash link (syllabus or next-lesson button) or when the module has one lesson. The 'offline app wiring' test calls onComplete on the captured props but never re-renders, so it misses this.

Pick the fallback 'first unfinished' lesson once at mount (for example `const [start] = useState(() => Math.max(0, data.lessons.findIndex((l) => !session.done().has(l.key))))`) and use it when the hash names no lesson. The planned model after the pilots splits identity from tenancy:
- users becomes the identity only (email, name, credentials, 2FA).
- A new memberships(user_id, tenant_id, role, status, department_id) table carries everything that is per tenant today. One person can then belong to several organisations (holding companies, consultants, vendor staff) without duplicate accounts.
